Who We Are

One path, built from four names

We are a Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering team in the BBI 3101 Biomedical Engineering Design I course. Our name comes from the first letters of our members' names. "Path" stands for a path that brings us together through unity, collaboration and a shared commitment to real healthcare challenges.

What We Stand For

Our Core Values

These values shape how we treat each other and how we approach every need statement, report and prototype.

Patient-Centred Innovation

Patients and their needs are at the centre of everything we design. We aim for practical, affordable and safe solutions suited to resource-limited settings in Uganda.

Accountability

We own our commitments, deadlines and mistakes, keep our promises, and raise difficulties early while taking the initiative to solve them.

Respect

We value each member's time, ideas and experience, keep the team inclusive, and keep disagreements about ideas, not people.

Collaboration

We succeed as one team: sharing knowledge, supporting each other and recognising every member's contribution fairly.

Integrity

We are honest and transparent in research, data, citations and peer reviews. We never plagiarise, misrepresent or fabricate results.

Excellence

We commit to high-quality need statements, prototypes, reports and presentations, welcome feedback and keep improving.

Effective Communication

We share progress, responsibilities, deadlines and decisions clearly, respectfully and promptly so everyone stays informed.

Where We Look

Strategic Focus Areas

Approved by Ms. Racheal Nalwoga on 1 September 2026 after four meetings of discussion and evidence. Each area has a team lead.

Maternal & Child Health

Uganda's maternal and neonatal mortality is high: 189 deaths per 100,000 live births and 22 per 1,000 live births.

Lead · Nuwamanya Oscar

Emergency Medicine

Time-critical care where equipment shortages and delays have immediate consequences.

Lead · Ssekitoleko Shafic

Trauma

Road-traffic injuries and fracture care carry a high burden and frequent complications.

Lead · Rwotokonya Emmanuel

Laboratory

Sample handling, testing quality and reliability underpin diagnosis across all specialties.

Lead · Khaitsa Margret

Final Need

Apnea in preterm babies

Our Final Need

"NICU nurses need a way for early detection of apnea in preterm babies for timely intervention."

Apnea of prematurity is a pause in breathing of 20 seconds or more, or a shorter pause with a slow heart rate or low oxygen. It happens because a premature baby's breathing system is not fully developed, and almost all babies born before 28 weeks have it. The need was accepted at our mid-semester presentation on 16 October 2026.

Gaps in current detection methods

Chest impedanceGives many false alarms
Pulse oximetryDetects low oxygen only after the apnea has happened
ECG monitoringInfers apnea indirectly from heart changes
Clinical observationUnreliable when nurses have a heavy workload
What's Next

Concept generation & selection

Ideate

Generate concepts

Brainstorming, mind mapping, morphological analysis, SCAMPER and TRIZ.

Select

Screen and compare

Must-have criteria, a Pugh matrix and a weighted decision matrix to pick one concept.

Deliver

Prototype and present

Low-fidelity bench prototype. Final presentation 25 November; final report 4 December.

How We Work

Team Rules & Policies

Meetings & attendance
  • Meetings start on time; members arrive a few minutes early.
  • The Chairperson sets dates and venues and gives 24 hours' notice.
  • Every meeting has an agenda; minutes are shared within 24 hours.
Tasks & deadlines
  • Tasks are shared fairly by role, focus area and workload.
  • Internal deadlines come before course deadlines to allow review.
  • All work is stored in a shared folder with version control.
Communication
  • The team WhatsApp group is the main channel for updates.
  • Members respond to important messages within 24 hours.
Decision-making

We aim for consensus. If that fails, a simple majority decides, and the Chairperson casts the deciding vote on a tie.

Conduct & conflict resolution

Conflicts go first to the members involved, then to the Chairperson and team, and finally to the course facilitators. No one takes credit for others' work, and all sources are cited.
